## Automated Status Summary
#### Scope
Auto-pilot's own formatter produces output that auto-pilot's own guard then rejects, and the pause that follows is permanent: the next run reformats the same body the same way and fails the same check. Nothing in the loop can clear it, and the issue keeps `status:in-progress`, which reads as healthy work rather than a stall.

Measured on 2026-09-13 in `stranske/Doc-Lineage`: **every one of the ten issues carrying `agents:auto-pilot` was paused this way**, each with the identical comment:

```
⚠️ Auto-pilot paused during formatting.
Formatter output does not satisfy the canonical issue-format contract.
```

The repository produced **zero implementation pull requests in nine days**. Its only merges were template sync, dependency sync, a scaffold rename and one belt bootstrap. Over the same nine days the eleven established repositories merged 297 pull requests and closed 209 issues, so this is specific to the loop, not to fleet capacity.

Two further details from the same comments:

- The dispatcher had already created `codex/issue-8` before the pause, so branches accumulate for work that never starts.
- The step banner posts as the literal string `🤖 Auto-pilot step $((STEP_COUNT + 1))`. The arithmetic is never expanded, so the step counter is inoperative and the comment is wrong on its face.

**Why this is a latch rather than a bug.** The pause state is indistinguishable from progress. The issue keeps an `agent:*` label and `status:in-progress`, no `needs-human` is applied, and no PR exists — so a sweep looking for frozen work sees a claimed, in-progress issue and moves on. That is exactly how nine days passed unnoticed.

<!-- Updated WORKFLOW_OUTPUTS.md context:start -->
## Context for Agent

### Related Issues/PRs
- [#3391](https://github.com/stranske/Workflows/issues/3391)
<!-- Updated WORKFLOW_OUTPUTS.md context:end -->

#### Tasks
- [ ] Reproduce with a body the formatter mangles: capture the formatter's output and the validator's rejection side by side, and record which rule fails.
- [ ] Fix the shell expansion so the step banner reports a real step number rather than `$((STEP_COUNT + 1))`.
- [ ] Give the pause an exit: on the first failure, re-run the formatter once; on a second identical failure, stop retrying and apply `needs-human` with the validator's exact rejection text in the comment, so the state is legible to both a person and a sweep.
- [ ] Release the lock when pausing: remove `status:in-progress` (and the `agent:*` claim) when auto-pilot gives up, so the opener lane can select the issue instead of treating it as claimed.
- [ ] Delete or reuse the branch the dispatcher created when the run never starts, so `codex/issue-<n>` branches do not accumulate against unstarted work.
- [ ] Report the counts together after every auto-pilot sweep — issues dispatched, formatted, paused, handed to a human — including zeros, so a run that paused everything is distinguishable from a run that did nothing.

#### Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A fixture body that fails the contract twice ends with `needs-human`, the validator's rejection quoted, and no `status:in-progress` remaining.
- [ ] The same fixture leaves no orphaned `codex/issue-<n>` branch.
- [ ] The step banner in a real run shows an integer.
- [ ] A well-formed body still passes formatting and dispatches, so the exit path does not block healthy work.
- [ ] The post-sweep summary prints all four counts including zeros.

<!-- auto-status-summary:end -->
title: fix: make auto-pilot formatter failure recoverable
